newsitem.title: USA: Citgo, union talk temporary deal at Illinois plant.
newsitem.headline: Citgo, union talk temporary deal at Illinois plant.

text.p: Citgo Petroleum Corp and local Oil Chemical and Atomic Workers Union (OCAW) officials at the company's Lemont, Illinois plant held talks Wednesday over a possible interim deal to ensure workers there are protected by an agreement until a dispute is worked out.

Citgo, an affiliate of PDV America Inc which is state owned Petroleos de Venezuela's main U.S. operating company, last week said it was looking to negotiate a new agreement with Lemont workers on the grounds that Citgo was not a party to a deal worked out last year after a bitter nine-month dispute.

"The company has taken the position that there is nothing in place. What we are trying to do is to agree an interim agreement with a life of 90 days to give our members some protection," said Dean Alexander, assistant to OCAW president Bob Wages and one of the negotiators of last year's deal.
Union officials say that Citgo is being disingenuous in claiming to be a "new" employer as its parent was a 50 percent owner in the plant and a co-signer to last year's agreement.

"We're in the courts now and going to continue that fight. In the meantime, we have to figure out some way to offer our members protection and we're saying, 'sit down and talk about an interim agreement,'" said Alexander.

The longer-term dispute will have to await a court ruling and hinges on the interpretation of the Burns Security Services versus National Labor Relations Board Supreme Court decision of 1972 which essentially allows a new owner to throw out a previously negotiated labor agreement.
The signatories to last year's agreement at the Lemont plant were the union and both of the the then 50-50 owners, Unocal Corp and PDV America.

In a deal which closed earlier this month, Unocal retained the joint-venture corporate entity, UNO-VEN, with $250 million in cash. PDV America created PDV MidWest Refining Inc as the corporate owner of the Lemont plant and other UNO-VEN assets and gave Citgo an operating contract for the Lemont refinery.
"We think we can prove that Citgo is a joint employer and required by law to honor the original agreement," said Alexander.
Citgo officials weren't immediately available for comment.
